draftContext.markdown:
The October 21 acceptance cycle (#416) remains the single blocking item. All four technical blockers have merged fixes as of this window. The next action is a manual trigger of the live provider run against the repaired pipeline; the specific command surface is the acceptance resume workflow introduced in #424. If the provider run fails, the synthetic probe (#428–430) should be run first to isolate schema-side vs. article-fit-side failure before any further code changes are attempted.

Post-token-count for the compacted evidence view (#427) is not yet in the record — it will be produced by the #416 run. The growth rate of evidence as articles accumulate is an open characterization question; #427 is a point fix, not a capacity model.

#421 (October 22 review DRAFT) exits on acceptance of the October 22 action review output, or closes without merge if the pipeline marks it resolved with no material findings.

morning-cockpit #60 has no activity across two windows and no stated dependency. Its disposition — merge, close, or park — is an owner gate with no technical blocker.

lego-village-pipeline #44, #45, #46 are analysis-only DRAFTs with no active blockers identified. Closing them vs. converting to issues is an owner decision; they are accumulating drift at 12+ days open.

classic-space-venue #4 is parallel work, not a dependency of the editorial pipeline. Its core issue dependencies (#544, #564–567) are wayfinder/world-building research; none are editorial-pipeline blockers.

API spend per failed acceptance cycle (~193K input tokens) is not published in this record. That cost dimension would make the compaction fix legible to anyone outside the immediate codebase.

The `DRAFT_CONTINUATION_CONTEXT` HTML comment block in the raw draft source is machine-readable pipeline state metadata. It is not reader-facing content and should not appear in any published form. Whether it is suppressed at render time or stripped before publication is a pipeline hygiene question for the next hardening pass.
